editorial:
Imagine feeling a huge void in your home because your kids moved away to the big city. That is exactly what Minago Iremadze is going through in this touching story. He and his wife are simple peasants who just want their family back together. One son is busy studying and the other has started a new life with a city girl. The vibe here is very quiet and emotional, focusing on the gap between old country traditions and the fast pace of modern city life. You will feel the ache in Minago's heart as he tries to convince his boys that home is where they truly belong.

What really works here is the acting, which feels very real and not forced. You can tell the filmmakers wanted you to feel the sadness of a father who is losing his grip on his children. While the pace is a bit slow, it helps you soak in the mood. If you enjoy slow-burn dramas about family, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older gem, try to find a high-quality restoration to stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best experience, or add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection to keep forever.
endingExplained: In the end, Minago has a heart-to-heart talk with his sons in the city. Even though the brothers love their father and understand his pain, they realize they cannot go back to the farm. They have grown too fond of city life and their new careers. The movie wraps up with a sad but honest realization that times change and children eventually grow apart from their parents' dreams. It is a bittersweet finish.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about family bonds and generational gaps.
